nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative algebra over a field $K$ and let $b$ be a $K$-basis of $R$ indexed by a finite set. Then the discriminant of $b$ over $K$ is nonzero if and only if $R$ is étale over $K$.
nodes.title: Étale algebras are detected by the discriminant

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative algebra over a field $K$ and let $b$ be a $K$-basis of $R$ indexed by a finite set. For $z \in R$ write $\operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(z)$ for the trace of the $K$-linear map given by multiplication by $z$. Then the discriminant of $b$ over $K$ is nonzero if and only if the trace form $(x, y) \mapsto \operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(xy)$ of $R$ over $K$ is nondegenerate.
nodes.title: Discriminant and nondegeneracy of the trace form

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative algebra over a field $K$ that is étale over $K$. Then for every $K$-basis $b$ of $R$ indexed by a finite set, the discriminant of $b$ over $K$ is nonzero.
nodes.title: Étale algebras have nonzero discriminant

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative algebra over a field $K$ and let $b$ be a $K$-basis of $R$ indexed by a finite set. If the discriminant of $b$ over $K$ is nonzero, then $R$ is étale over $K$.
nodes.title: A nonzero discriminant forces étaleness

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative algebra over a field $K$. For $z \in R$ write $\operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(z)$ for the trace of the $K$-linear map given by multiplication by $z$, taken to be $0$ when $R$ is infinite-dimensional over $K$. If the trace form $(x, y) \mapsto \operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(xy)$ of $R$ over $K$ is nondegenerate, then $R$ is reduced, that is, its only nilpotent element is $0$.
nodes.title: A nondegenerate trace form forces the algebra to be reduced

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field extension of $K$, and $A$ a commutative $K$-algebra that is finite-dimensional over $K$. If the ring $\Omega \otimes_K A$ is semisimple, then $A$ is étale over $K$.
nodes.title: Étale criterion via semisimple base change

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative algebra over a field $K$, and for $z \in R$ write $\operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(z)$ for the trace of the $K$-linear map given by multiplication by $z$, taken to be $0$ when $R$ is infinite-dimensional over $K$. If $x, y \in R$ and $x$ is nilpotent, then the trace form of $R$ over $K$ vanishes at $(x, y)$, that is, $\operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(xy) = 0$.
nodes.title: Nilpotent elements pair to zero under the trace form
